stem: Atoms contain the subatomic particles electrons, protons and neutrons. Protons and electrons were discovered by observations of their behaviours in electric fields.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
The diagram shows the behaviour of separate beams of electrons and protons in an electric field.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Complete the diagram with the relative charge of each of the electrically charged plates.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: On the diagram, draw a line to show how a separate beam of neutrons from the same source behaves in the same electric field.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Electrons in atoms up to $_{36}\text{Kr}$ are distributed in s, p and d orbitals.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:

parts.label: (b)(iii)
(b)(iv)
parts.text:
The first ionisation energies of elements in the first row of the d block ($_{21}\text{Sc}$ to $_{29}\text{Cu}$) are very similar. For all these elements, it is a 4s electron that is lost during the first ionisation.

Suggest why the first ionisation energies of these elements are very similar.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
*Hydron* is a general term used to represent the ions $_{1}^{1}\text{H}^{+}$, $_{1}^{2}\text{H}^{+}$ and $_{1}^{3}\text{H}^{+}$.

State, in terms of subatomic particles in the nucleus, what is the same about each of these ions and what is different.
